lead: Meta Platforms / FB — the metaverse bill comes due
smaller: PayPal / PYPL — the worst day ever tests capitulation
Spotify / SPOT — the boycott meets the subscriber count
Advanced Micro Devices / AMD — the beat-and-raise that held its gains
why_lead: Meta Platforms (FB) is the day's largest new crowd event: Reuters reported shares sinking 20% after hours as Facebook lost daily users for the first time (n0846, Guardian n1138), with a $10 billion iOS privacy revenue hit (n0822) and $10 billion of metaverse spending (n1151, n1149, Reality Labs $3.3 billion Q4 loss n1137). The completed 2 February session (323.00 USD, +1.25% 1-session, +9.63% 5-session) shows the stock was bid into the print; only the after-hours reaction is known, so the 3 February session is treated as the pending test. Attention evidence is the retail metaverse mania (Snoop Dogg neighbour $450,000 n0980; metaverse real estate $500 million n0960) and the ticker rebrand (n1136); smart money is split between Wall Street's trillions thesis and analysts' $3 billion revenue estimate (n0343, n1020) and Arnault's bubble warning and Bloomberg's woo-Wall-Street critique (n0277, n1170). Relation to strictly earlier retail notes (2022-02-01 GameStop lead; 2022-02-02 Alphabet lead): new ticker and new narrative; Alphabet's +7.52% split-day session appears only as the contrast in What Is Driving It, and Netflix (a 2022-02-01 smaller item) appears only as the Historical Analog with own-date Barron's evidence (n0293) and card moves.
why_smaller: PayPal / PYPL: material update of the 2022-02-02 smaller item. That item flagged the post-results plunge as pending; newly published own-date evidence shows the completed outcome — worst-ever trading day, -24% (CNBC n0860; card -24.59% to 132.57 USD), over $50 billion of value lost (n0857), the account-growth goal scrapped (n0859), 4.5 million illegitimate accounts (n1156), disappointing guidance (WSJ n0858) — and the narrative changes from 'trapdoor' to 'capitulation or falling knife', with contagion to Block, Shopify and Affirm on the card.

Spotify / SPOT: material update of the 2022-02-01 smaller item, whose stated break test was the next quarterly results. Those results are now out: 180 million paying subscribers (n1160), 406 million MAUs (n1161), and Reuters reported the stock sinking on weaker-than-expected first-quarter subscriber numbers (n0872); Jefferies' 'air pocket' view (n1169), Eve 6 (n1154) and the CEO on Rogan (n1159) define where it breaks. The narrative changes from 'buy the boycott' to 'the boycott meets the subscriber count'.

Advanced Micro Devices / AMD: new item with a distinct beat-and-raise narrative — +10% after hours on a strong 2022 outlook (n0642), confirmed by the completed session (+5.12% to 122.76 USD; SOXL +7.47%), Lisa Su (n1124), record-earnings expectation (n1125) and BofA's Arya seeing earnings potentially doubling or tripling (n1168); breaks on the rate path (2Y context), the chip-shortage boom-bust worry (n0856) and leveraged-ETF exposure.
considered_not_chosen: Alphabet / GOOGL (+7.52% to 2,960.00 USD; Reuters 'split may trigger retail buying, Dow inclusion' n0782; Bloomberg n0781; Pelosi windfall n0783): the 2022-02-02 lead; used only as contrast in the Meta lead rather than repeated as an item, to avoid recycling the split story.

GameStop / GME (-11.15% to 100.04 USD; Reuters on Roaring Kitty n0778; PFOF $3.8 billion n0881): the 2022-02-01 lead's anniversary bounce reversed, but the new evidence is retrospective; held back to keep four distinct narratives.

Wormhole hack ($325 million, Elliptic n0970; CNBC n0977) with SOL -7.40% and BTC -4.62%: no own-date headline ties the exploit to a specific token on the card, so a token-level item would rest on an unsupported link.
Henry Hub natural gas (+15.79% 1-session; Texas bitcoin miners powering down n0971, n0973): a weather trade without retail-attention evidence.

Amazon, Snap, Pinterest and Ford results due 3 February and the ECB/BoE decisions are pending after the cutoff; Amazon appears only as a previewed pending catalyst (n0784) and the BoE only via 'expected rate hike' (n0107).

Feb 2-stamped items were checked for after-cutoff risk; the Meta, PayPal, Spotify, AMD and Wormhole items describe events completed before 00:00 UTC on 3 February, and none describing the 3 February session were used.
